title: Introduce replayable dialogue corpus seeder and tail stability reporter
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: We need a compact, seedable dialogue corpus and an associated stability reporter to make tail-regression detection deterministic across CI runs and local experiments. Current benchmark runs produce non-reproducible tails due to randomized augmentations and non-deterministic tokenization order when sampling multimodal prompts. This PR introduces a replayable corpus format, a seedable augmentation pipeline, and a tail stability reporter that computes run-to-run drift metrics (p95/p99/p999 and Wasserstein distance) and emits a lightweight artifact used by regression alerts.

What this PR contains: 1) corpus format: a small compact binary+json index (corpus.bin + index.json) that stores canonical tokenization seeds and deterministic RNG states per dialogue; 2) seeder library: replay_seeder.py (python) and a thin Go runner shim to produce deterministic batches for multi-language runners; 3) augmentation: deterministic_augmenter that accepts a 64-bit seed and applies reproducible paraphrase/noise transforms using the seeded RNG; 4) reporter: tail_stability_reporter (Rust) that ingests benchmark traces and computes delta metrics against a baseline artifact; 5) CI integration: a new workflow and helper that uploads baseline artifacts to the perf-artifacts S3 bucket and gates merges on no-regression or an explicit override.

How to run locally: 
- python3 tools/replay_seeder.py --corpus=corpus/index.json --seed=0xDEADBEEF --out=fixtures/replay_batches.tar.gz
- ./bin/dialogue_runner --batches fixtures/replay_batches.tar.gz --backend local --out traces/run-20260112.json
- cargo run --bin tail_stability_reporter --baseline artifacts/baseline-20260101.json --run traces/run-20260112.json --out reports/drift-20260112.json

Checklist: [x] deterministic corpus format and reader; [x] seeded augmentation pipeline with unit tests; [x] example fixture and runner shim; [x] reporter outputs both numeric summary and compact artifact for CI; [x] CI job to bake baseline on demand.

Results summary from internal validation (single A100, 1k dialogues): baseline vs seeded-run (seed changed): p95 drift +0.4ms, p99 drift +2.1ms, p999 drift +9.3ms, Wasserstein(latency)=0.9. The reporter also surfaced a subtle microburst correlation in one cohort; that cohort is now flagged in the baseline artifact metadata so future runs can apply cohort-aware comparisons.

Notes and limitations: the binary corpus format is intentionally compact; it trades off human readability for deterministic token alignment. We document converters (tools/export_to_human_readable.py) to inspect content. The seeded augmentation currently includes paraphrase templates; we plan to add learned paraphrasers behind a determinism shim in a follow-up.

Related: ENG-4812 (repro benchmark infra), ENG-4920 (tail alerting design).

review_thread: Ravi Narayanan: Nice work — concept looks solid. Two asks: (1) add a short term migration note for existing baselines, (2) make the reporter output a machine-readable summary (JSON) alongside the human table.
Elena Park: PTAL — added migration notes in docs and ensured reporter writes reports/drift-summary.json. Also added intentional hashes to baseline artifacts for quick validation.
Marta Hsu: The seeded augmenter is great; a nit about template variability: could we surface the template list in logs so we can replay which transforms hit a sample?
Elena Park: Done — augmenter now logs applied template ids to the trace metadata under augmentation.template_ids.
Leo Vargas: CI integration LGTM. On perf numbers, we should add a small canary in the workflow that replays a known slow cohort to catch microburst regressions earlier.
Elena Park: Added canary cohort selection as an optional step in perf_replay.yml (off by default).
